_meta.description: Authoritative predicate-vocabulary registry. Each entry declares the canonical predicate string, its cardinality, a human-readable description, and the registry version when the entry was added. Shape: { _meta: {...}, entries: [ { predicate, cardinality, description, added_version } ] }.

entries.description: Rationale or grounds accepted in support of a decision or rule; multiple grounds may apply simultaneously
Trigger or condition that activates a component; multiple activators may be valid at once
Mechanism by which a subject was added to the system
Current affirmation status of an assertion or rule
Context or scope in which a rule or pattern is applied; may apply in multiple contexts
Scope or entity to which a rule or constraint applies; may apply to multiple targets
Plural identity or collective attribute assertion; multiple objects may be simultaneously asserted
Safety classification flag indicating whether a set of operations is safe outside the claude-memory project boundary
Behavioral characteristic of a component; multiple behaviors may be simultaneously described
Blocker preventing a subject from progressing; a subject may have multiple simultaneous blockers
Current existence state of a named git branch; subject is the branch name, object is 'exists' or '<absent>'. Volatile now-state: re-probed live at serve time via the L3 reality-check registry.
Information or event that a component captures or records; multiple captured items may apply
Issue, event, or defect caught by a mechanism; multiple caught items may apply
Recorded decision or choice made by a subject

Whether a specific commit SHA is merged (reachable as an ancestor of a ref or HEAD); object is 'merged', '<not-merged>', or '<sha> on <branch>'. Volatile now-state: re-probed live at serve time. Excludes is_at_commit and shipped_at (historical then-state).
Refactor note associated with a cmdDrop operation
Convergence status: records that a process or review has reached a stable conclusion
Scope or topics that a document, test, or spec covers; multiple covered items may apply
Author or mechanism that created a subject
Current position, value, or state of a subject at the time of assertion
Default value or behavior for a configuration point or parameter
Default value or target that a parameter or option resolves to when not explicitly set
Authoritative definition of a term or concept
Work items or features delivered by a sprint, bundle, or session; multiple deliverables apply simultaneously
Subject depends on the named object; multiple objects are valid simultaneously
Target level or role to which a subject is elevated
Policies or constraints that a component enforces; may enforce multiple simultaneously
The point in time or processing stage at which a check or rule evaluates
Classification flag indicating a result is a false positive
Events or conditions on which a hook or trigger fires; multiple events may apply
Version, commit, or release in which a defect was fixed
Bug or defect found in a component; a subject may have multiple bugs recorded
Git behavioral quirk or workaround note; multiple quirks may apply to a subject
General possession or association; a subject may have multiple objects
Artifact associated with a subject; multiple artifacts may exist simultaneously
Defect present in a component; a component may have multiple simultaneous defects

Current packaging state of the working tree at close time: 'clean' when all session work is committed and pushed, or a description of unpackaged state (dirty working tree, commits ahead of upstream). Supersedes prior session row so the close record is always true to itself.
Records that a file or document was updated and what the update covered; a subject may accrue multiple distinct updates over time
File path where a subject is defined or located; a subject may be defined or present in multiple files simultaneously
Items included within a set or scope; multiple included items apply simultaneously
Identity or classification assertion; a subject may simultaneously hold multiple valid class memberships or identity labels
Current git commit SHA or reference for a subject
The authoritative database for a given domain or subject
Blocker that prevents a subject from completing; legacy synonym for blocked_by — normalize via migration
Agent or action that clears a block or condition on a subject
A constraint that applies to a subject or system behavior; multiple constraints may apply simultaneously
Design intent or target use-case for a component; multiple use-cases can be simultaneously valid
Strategic or architectural direction for a subject
Precise value or identity for a subject, stronger than is; one exact value applies
Current model (AI or data model) in use for a subject
Negation: identifies agents or mechanisms that do not apply a rule; multiple non-applying agents may be simultaneously valid
Notes that a heuristic or mechanism is over-tuned for one or more patterns simultaneously; multiple over-tuning targets can be simultaneously valid
Agent or mechanism that sets a value for a subject; multiple sources (e.g., env, config, CLI) can be simultaneously valid setters under a precedence model
Current status of a project entity
Current value of a configuration parameter or setting
Port or interface on which a service listens; a service may listen on multiple ports or interfaces simultaneously
Filesystem or network location of a resource; a resource may exist at multiple simultaneous locations
The matching algorithm specification or reference for a subject
Definitional statement of what a term or concept means; a term may carry multiple simultaneously-valid meanings or definitional facets
Destination to which a subject has been moved or relocated
Normative requirement; a subject may have multiple simultaneous obligations
Definitional constraint specifying what a term or phrase must mean in context
Prohibition; items a subject must never use; multiple prohibitions may apply
Items that a set or scope no longer includes; multiple removed items may apply
Items newly included in a scope after a change; multiple new inclusions may apply simultaneously
Current tool or mechanism in use after a transition, superseding prior usage; normalize legacy rows to uses via migration
A session-driving open thread / next-action persisted as a queryable row; one live thread per thread-key (subject)
Constraint that a subject is limited to an orchestration role only
Source or origin from which a subject originates; a subject can originate from multiple upstream sources simultaneously
The ordering constraint for phases in a multi-phase operation
Policy statement applicable to a subject; multiple policies may apply simultaneously

Current GitHub pull request state; subject must contain the PR number (e.g. 'PR #92'), object is 'open', 'closed', or 'merged'. Volatile now-state: re-probed live at serve time via gh CLI (fail-soft to unverifiable when gh is absent/offline).
Stated preference of a subject
Session quick-reference pointer block persisted as a queryable row; latest supersedes prior
Scope or framing of the roadmap section in a README
Resources or files that a component reads; multiple read sources may apply
Prerequisites or requirements for a subject; multiple requirements may apply simultaneously
Values or types returned by a function or query; multiple return types may apply
Current state of a schema migration
The session TL;DR persisted as a queryable row; latest supersedes prior
Specific commit or tag at which a feature was shipped
Bundle, version, or PR in which a feature was shipped; a feature may ship across multiple bundles
Normative guidance (weaker than must_do); multiple guidance items may apply simultaneously
Conditions or contexts under which a step or rule should be skipped; multiple skip conditions may apply
Records that a process or step was skipped and why
Arguments accepted by a command or function; multiple arguments may be accepted
Event or condition that triggers a behavior; multiple triggers may apply simultaneously
Primary usage pattern or description for a command or component
Legacy alias for chose — user-stated choice; normalize to chose via migration
Flag or reference indicating that a behavior or setting was explicitly directed by the user
Tools, libraries, or components that a subject uses; multiple simultaneous uses are valid
Database that a component uses as its primary backing store
